title: Intent/Application spec
description: The desired-state payload for an application Intent (charter §2.4, ADR-0023). v3 adds `chartVersion` for the CHART delivery form (ADR-0148 follow-up b). A SIBLING VERSION rather than an edit to v2, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN STYLISTIC: v2 was edited in place first, on the argument that adding a NEW typed property is not the 'tightening' this file's header warns about — no declaration in the repo used the key, so nothing that parsed stopped parsing. `task ci` agreed, because the unit tests re-derive every hash from the shipped files and a self-consistent edit is invisible to them. The live floor did not: strattd refused to start with 'contract drift: intents/application v2 is pinned to 02c02872… but the shipped document hashes to d342b698… — publish a new version, never mutate a pin (§1.5)'. The pin is over the DOCUMENT, not over the compatibility of the change, and that is the whole point of it — a reviewer reasoning about whether an edit is breaking is exactly what a hash exists to stop being load-bearing. The resolver keys by kind and takes the newest, so v1/v2 stay as pin rows for history while v3 is what validates. Still deliberately OPEN (additionalProperties: true): Intent/Application is a generic kind whose spec carries application-specific values — the app-cert demo's commonName, for instance — and closing it would force core to know every application's configuration fields, the ontology creep §1.1 and §9 forbid. Blueprints reference spec fields by explicit lookup ({{.spec.package}}).

chartVersion.description: Desired version of the deliverable for a CHART-delivered application, as a STRING — the same load-bearing type argument `port` records: contracts/facets/app.deliverable declares the OBSERVED version as a string and nothing coerces between types (ADR-0118 D1), so the desired and observed values must share a type or they are never comparable. Typed here rather than left to additionalProperties because a shipping Blueprint route reads it (estate/blueprints/podinfo.yaml).

port.description: Desired listen port, as a STRING — the type is load-bearing, not stylistic. contracts/facets/app.config.schema.json declares the OBSERVED port as a string, and a compiled expectation from this spec is compared against that observed value; nothing coerces between types (ADR-0118 D1), so the two must agree or they are never comparable. Typed here because two shipping Blueprint routes read it (estate/blueprints/web-server.yaml and the app-cert demo) — and because leaving it untyped cost a full cluster round-trip: an Intent declaring a number parsed cleanly and failed only at facet write-back with '/port: got number, want string'.
